ordered_diagnoses: KRAS Wild-Type Rectal Adenocarcinoma with Metastases

facts.raw_span: A man in his 40s
weighing 109kg
stage IV KRAS wild-type rectal adenocarcinoma diagnosed in November 2013
pulmonary and liver metastases
radiation therapy and multiple chemotherapy cycles
a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias on his lower right lateral shin
the lesion was not associated with pain or pruritus
Discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels were observed, with superficial, small lobules of small-caliber vessels
the epidermis was normal
KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R identified as the only somatic mutation

concepts.why: The patient developed a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias on his lower right lateral shin, which is consistent with cutaneous telangiectasia.
The patient received radiation therapy, which is a known risk factor for developing telangiectasia, and the lesion developed after radiation therapy.

concepts.preferred_label: KRAS Wild-Type Rectal Adenocarcinoma with Metastases
concepts.why: The patient was diagnosed with stage IV KRAS wild-type rectal adenocarcinoma and had pulmonary and liver metastases, which is consistent with this diagnosis.
The patient was found to have a somatic KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R mutation, which is a genetic variant that may be associated with the development of telangiectasia.
The patient received multiple chemotherapy cycles, which is a known risk factor for developing vascular lesions, and the lesion developed after chemotherapy.
The patient developed a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias, which is consistent with telangiectasia macularis eruptiva perstans.
The patient developed a vascular lesion that does not fit into a specific category, which may be an atypical vascular lesion.
The patient developed a vascular lesion that may be a vascular tumor, such as a hemangioma.

rationales.F03: KRAS wild-type rectal adenocarcinoma is a specific type of cancer, which rules in C03.
rationales.F06: The presence of a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias is a characteristic feature of cutaneous telangiectasia, which rules in C01.
rationales.F08: The histopathological findings of discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels and superficial, small lobules of small-caliber vessels are consistent with cutaneous telangiectasia, which rules in C01.
rationales.F10: The presence of a somatic KDR (VEGFR2) mutation is a specific genetic finding that rules in C04.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of radiation therapy and the development of a well-defined, blanchable red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias support Radiation-Induced Telangiectasia as the most likely diagnosis.
